tools.description: Send a message to a direct continuable child by its agent id. If you are a resident continuable child, you may also target your direct parent. If the target is still working, the message steers its nearest step; if it is idle, the message starts a turn. This call returns no answer from the agent — only confirmation that the message was delivered. A failure means the message was NOT delivered.

tools.description: Copy a remote FILE from a configured SSH host to this machine (the dsh host). Use this only when the source is on the remote host; files already on this machine are read with the local file tools (read / write / edit), not ssh_download. Directory download is not supported — download files individually. Triggers: download file from server, fetch remote log/artifact.

Prefer combining independent read-only queries into one command. Triggers: run command on server, deploy, check server/status, service control, view logs, any remote operation.

tools.name: subagent
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task to a subagent (a separate agent that works in its own context) to offload focused, independent work — research, a scoped implementation, an analysis — so it does not consume this conversation's context. The subagent returns its result, not its intermediate steps. Give it a complete, standalone prompt: it does not see this conversation. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

prompt.description: The complete, self-contained task for the subagent. It does not share this conversation's context, so include everything it needs.

tools.name: subagent_fork
tools.description: Delegate a task to a subagent that inherits this conversation: a child agent seeded with all completed turns so far (it does not see the current in-flight turn). Use this when the subtask builds on this conversation's context — a follow-up analysis, a review, a continuation — without consuming this conversation's context for the work itself. You receive its result, not its intermediate steps. This tool runs in the background by default, immediately returns a durable subagent id, and keeps the child conversation available for later turns. When that run settles, the runtime sends the parent a notice containing its outcome and any final assistant message; `send_message` steers the child's nearest step while it is running and starts a turn while it is idle. Set `run_in_background: false` only when your next action depends on receiving the result.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the delegated task, for display.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent. It already sees this conversation's completed turns, so build on them freely and state only what is new.

run_in_background.description: Whether to run in the background and return a durable subagent id immediately. Defaults to true. Set false to wait for the result when your next action depends on it.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: web_search
tools.description: Search the web for current information. Provide 1–4 queries in the required queries array. Returns an optional summary answer and a list of source URLs.

queries.description: Required search queries; accepts 1–4 items and merges their results.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

The workflow's identity rides the `meta` parameter as JSON: required `name` (short kebab-case) and `description` strings, optional `whenToUse` string and `phases` array (`{title, detail?, provider?, model?}`). The `script` parameter is the plain JavaScript body ONLY (NOT TypeScript, and NO `export const meta` statement — meta is a parameter, not code), running with top-level await; end with `return <value>` — the value must be JSON-serializable and is this tool's result.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf — no pattern/format/numeric bounds) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides (either may be provided alone). Anything else (`effort`/`isolation`/`agentType`) is rejected loudly.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. An ordinary stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) throw errors that ALWAYS kill the script — they never dissolve into a per-item `null`.

Constraints: concurrency and total-agent caps apply; no filesystem, network, timers, or Node.js APIs are provided — the agents do the work, the script only coordinates them. The run executes in the foreground: this call returns when the whole script finishes.

script.description: The plain-JS workflow script body (top-level await allowed; NO `export const meta` statement; end with `return <json-value>`).

meta.description: The workflow identity block (plain JSON — never code).

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

justification.description: Required with sandbox_permissions: one sentence for the user explaining why this exact file operation needs the wider access.

71:   const tail = max - head

PLAN REVIEWER (momus) — adversarial REQUIREMENTS INTERROGATION for "rename a workmate + delete a workmate" (repo /root/dshProj/my-power-dsh). Read-only; read src/index.ts (439L), web-client.js, members.js, tests, QA scripts. No plan proposed.

## (1) USER QUESTIONS — only the human can decide

Q1 AUTHORITY / SURFACE. Should rename+delete be agent-callable tools (`mpd_workmate_rename`/_delete), GUI-only human actions, or both?
- Why: the library is the agent's own durable cross-project memory; an agent tool lets any captain/teammate autonomously destroy months of evolved persona+memory. Also relevant: AGENTS.md §6 forbids plugins writing outside the workspace EXCEPT this library — the write authority question is genuinely product-level.
- Candidates: (a) both, tools exist but destructive call requires an explicit `confirm:"<name>"` argument; (b) both, unguarded; (c) GUI-only (no agent tools at all); (d) tools only, no GUI change.

Q2 DELETE REVERSIBILITY. Hard `rm -rf` or recoverable?
- Why: memory.md is accumulated evidence that cannot be regenerated from the base template; a mis-click permanently loses it. Also index.json / any future consumer.
- Candidates: (a) hard delete; (b) move to `~/.mpd/workmate/.trash/<name>-<ISO>/` (restorable, hidden from list); (c) rename-to-tombstone + keep dir, hidden; (d) hard delete but behind a typed-name confirmation.

Q3 RENAME SEMANTIC SCOPE. What exactly must move, and does the workmate's own text follow?
- Why: the name is embedded in artifacts — `autoNote()` writes `<baseName>-based workmate "<name>".` into note.md, and persona/memory may quote the old name in agent-written text. Silent drift confuses both the matching score and the human.
- Candidates: (a) dir + meta.name + index key only (stale note text accepted); (b) also rewrite the auto-note self-reference; (c) also append a `## Renamed <old> → <new>` memory entry and/or a `previousNames`/`renamedFrom` field so continuity is visible; (d) grep-replace the old name inside persona/memory. Plus: does rename bump `updatedAt` (it re-sorts the list) and does it count as a `uses` bump? (No.)

Q4 LIVE TEAM-MEMBER BINDING. What happens when the renamed/deleted workmate's name equals a member of a live or archived team?
- Why: binding is name-equality only — `packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/lib/members.js#workmateBacking` hashes the member name to the dir; the team file persists that member name. A rename silently strips the backing from a running member; a delete does the same; afterwards that member's `mpd_workmate_reflect` FAILS (ensureInstance throws "no workmate named"). Highest-risk case: a workmate named exactly a roster normal name (e.g. `senior-engineer`) is auto-bound to EVERY member called "Senior Engineer" in every `mpd`-profile team.
- Candidates: (a) silent (member keeps the already-injected persona; later reflect errors); (b) pre-check `.mpd/team/*/team.json` and REFUSE while a live team has such a member; (c) warn in the response and proceed; (d) cascade — rewrite team member names for rename (delete cannot cascade).
- Related sub-decision: for a rename, does the member follow automatically (alias) or must the user re-add the member?

Q5 OLD NAME AFTER RENAME (REUSE + IDENTITY SWAP). Is the old name freed immediately?
- Why: if freed, a later `mpd_workmate_init` can create a *different* workmate under the old name and every existing team member named that way silently re-binds to the new persona/memory — an invisible identity swap.
- Candidates: (a) free immediately; (b) reserve/tombstone in index.json (old name resolves as an alias to the new one; member binding follows the alias); (c) free but record a tombstone so `init` warns "name previously used by X".

Q6 NAME INPUT CONTRACT FOR RENAME. Strict-reject or silent-normalize, and are non-ASCII names supported?
- Why: `sanitizeName()` lowercases, kebab-cases, strips everything outside `[a-z0-9_-]` — a Chinese name such as 助理 sanitizes to "" and `wmDir("")` is the LIBRARY ROOT, so an unguarded empty key can target/recurse the whole library. Since the requester writes Chinese, they may expect CJK names — supporting them means changing the key scheme in BOTH plugins (members.js `workmateKey` must stay byte-identical).
- Candidates: (a) strict: reject invalid/empty/no-op/colliding names with a clear error (CJK unsupported, documented); (b) silent sanitize + error only on empty/collision; (c) allow Unicode dir names (new key scheme, cross-plugin change); (d) sanitize + auto-suffix like init's `base-N` when the name is empty or taken. Also decide: rename to the same sanitized name = error or 200 no-op? Collision with an existing workmate = refuse or merge?

Q7 GUI BEHAVIOR. Where do the controls live and how is delete confirmed?
- Why: this is the actual human-facing half of the request ("可以改名 / 可以删除"); the tab is DSH-better-sidebar-only, `single: true`, and its dictionaries are zh+en with zh as key-set source of truth (both must land in the same change, and `client.js` must be rebuilt or the tab shows nothing new).
- Candidates: (a) buttons in the detail view only; (b) inline per-row controls in the list; (c) native confirm / typed-name confirm / two-step (arm-then-confirm) for delete; and after rename: does the open detail view follow to the new name or return to the list? Undo/toast, or none?

Q8 SCOPE OF THE TRAVERSAL-DISCOVERED DEFECT. The deny lists in mpd-workmate-plugin (line 30) AND mpd-roles-plugin (line 23-27) name tools this harness does not have (`str_replace_editor`, `apply_patch`), and the harness rejects the whole restriction call — so read-only workmate spawn and `mpd_role_spawn` fail today. In this change or not?
- My recommendation for the user to rule on: OUT of scope (separate `fix/` branch per AGENTS.md §5) — different package, different failure mode, minimal-diff principle §2.6. Caveat that argues for IN: with the defect live, a readonly workmate cannot be spawned at all, so end-to-end acceptance evidence for rename/delete on readonly instances is unreachable.
- Candidates: (a) separate defect branch (recommended); (b) same change, both plugins; (c) same change, only the workmate plugin's list.

## (2) EDGE CASES THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST HANDLE
- EMPTY SANITIZED NAME: `sanitizeName(x) === ""` (e.g. CJK, punctuation-only, whitespace) must be rejected BEFORE any fs call — `wmDir("")` is `~/.mpd/workmate` itself, so delete would target the library root and rename would move it.
- Path containment: the resolved target must be a strict child of the library root and must not be `index.json` or any non-directory entry.
- Unknown name → explicit error, zero side effects; delete must not silently "succeed"; a second delete must error.
- Half-created / corrupt instance: a dir under the root with no meta.json (crash between `mkdirSync` and the meta write at init) — `listInstances` skips it, so rename/delete must decide: error, or allow cleanup of the orphan dir.
- Rename collision: target name already exists (or a *file* of that name exists) → refuse, mirroring init's `already exists` error.
- Sanitization collision: two distinct inputs mapping to the same key ("Alice Cooper" vs "alice-cooper" vs "Alice  Cooper").
- Case-only rename: "Alice" → "alice" is a sanitize-no-op on a case-insensitive filesystem — must be a defined outcome, not a rename-to-itself ENOENT.
- index.json consistency: it has NO reader today (`indexPath()`/`writeIndexEntry` are the only references — verified by grep), yet rename must remove the old key and add the new one, and delete must drop the key, or the file becomes permanently stale; also decide whether index.json is authoritative at all.
- Atomicity/partial failure: rename across the same fs is one `renameSync`, but meta.name + index write can fail after the dir moved → must not leave a dir whose name and meta.name disagree; delete must not leave a half-removed dir (nested persona/memory files).
- Symlinks: a workmate dir that is a symlink (or contains one) must not let delete/rename escape the library root.
- Race with in-flight work: `mpd_workmate_spawn` reads persona/memory then the subagent calls `mpd_workmate_reflect` LATER, while `reflect` does readMeta → mutate → `writeFileSync(join(wmDir(meta.name)...))`. A reflect racing a rename recreates the OLD directory (name resurrection); a reflect after delete throws. Must be a defined outcome (reject-in-flight vs last-writer-wins).
- Service consistency: `mpdWorkmate.get(old)` must return null and `.get(new)`/`.read(new)` the full detail immediately after the mutation; `list` must reflect it on the very next call (no caching).
- Cross-module: team-member backing (`members.js`) resolves merely by dir existence — after rename the member loses backing silently, and a workmate whose key equals a roster normal name (`senior-engineer`, `deep-worker`) affects every team using that member name.
- Readonly instances: their persona says "never modify anything" — rename/delete are library-admin ops, not workmate self-edits; the agent-tool path must not be usable by a readonly workmate to mutate the library.
- Web routes: method guard (405 on wrong verb), 400 on invalid JSON, 404 on unknown name (mirror the existing `/get` route's 404 shape), `cache-control: no-store`, and no absolute `$HOME` path leaking in the response (note: `initWorkmate` already returns `path`, so decide deliberately rather than by accident).
- Route/plugin lifecycle: routes are registered lazily via `ctx.get("webServer" ?? "httpServer")` behind `webRegistered`; a headless profile has no routes at all — rename/delete must still work tool-only.
- GUI: stale selection after mutation (detail must not keep polling a deleted/old name and must not 404-loop); the `single: true` tab must not open a second tab; new zh AND en keys are mandatory (zh is the key-set source of truth) and `node scripts/build-mpd-client.mjs` must be re-run or the shipped `client.js` shows nothing.
- Names that collide with the roster base ids/normal names and with existing workmate auto-names (`hephaestus-1`) — dedupe/auto-suffix logic must not overwrite.
- Deletion must not be reachable by the agent through `mpd_workmate_reflect`/`init` side effects (e.g. reflect on a missing name must not "recreate" the instance).
- Docs/tests to keep in sync (not optional, they are gates): package README.md + README.zh-CN.md, docs/user-guide.md + .zh-CN, AGENTS.md workmate tool list/glossary/troubleshooting, the preset text (`presets/mpd/agent.cordis.yml` + the `mpd` roster profile protocol string in `packages/mpd-bundle/cordis.patch.yml`), the QA self-tests that string-match the workmate source/routes (`skills/dsh-qa/scripts/workmate-library.mjs` asserts the list/roster/get route literals; `web-client-adapt.mjs` asserts list+init), and `packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/test/sidebar-tab.test.mjs`.

## (3) INVARIANTS ACCEPTANCE MUST PIN
I1 NAME↔DIR↔INDEX BIJECTION AND ROOT SAFETY. For every workmate at all times: `sanitizeName(meta.name)` === dir basename === the index.json key; after a rename the old key and old dir are gone; and no operation may ever resolve to, move, or recursively remove the library root itself — an empty/invalid sanitized name is rejected with zero side effects. (Pins the `wmDir("")===root` hazard; must hold identically in both plugins via the byte-identical `sanitizeName`/`workmateKey` algorithm.)
I2 RENAME IS IDENTITY-PRESERVING, NEVER A RE-INSTANTIATION. Rename carries the exact same instance: persona.md / memory.md / note.md content and length caps, `uses`, `lastTask`, `createdAt` all preserved (only the explicitly-decided self-references/`renamedFrom` metadata change); no base re-copy, no memory reset, no `uses` bump — a renamed workmate is byte-for-byte the same evolved agent under a new key.
I3 DELETE IS COMPLETE AND ALL-OR-NOTHING. After a successful delete: the instance dir is gone, its index entry is gone, `mpdWorkmate.get`/`read` return null, `list` no longer contains it, and NO other workmate's bytes changed; for an unknown/empty/invalid name the operation fails with a clear error and zero side effects; a failed delete never leaves a partially removed instance.
I4 CROSS-MODULE BINDING OUTCOME IS DETERMINISTIC AND TEST-PINNED. Whatever Q4/Q5 decide (silent / refuse / alias / cascade), the observable result for a team member whose name equals a mutated workmate, and for the `mpdWorkmate` service + `mpd_workmate_list`/`_match` views, must be exactly that decision at all times — no state where the dir, index.json, the service view and the member's injected backing disagree — and a test must pin it (offline lifecycle test in packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/test/workmate.test.ts + a QA self-test/real-boot row), with the real $HOME untouched (sandbox HOME).

Gate reminders for acceptance: `bun test`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test:qa`, `node scripts/verify-vendor.mjs`, `dsh --profile headless --dump-config` in an isolated DSH_HOME, evidence under evidence/<domain>/<slug>/<timestamp>/, bilingual docs in the same commit.

Rename/delete silently strips the backing; that member's later `mpd_workmate_reflect` then FAILS (`ensureInstance` throws). - agent-teams exposes NO cordis service (no `provide(` found for team state) — only tools `agent_teams_*`. So a cross-plugin cascade of team member names has no sanctioned API from within the workmate plugin. That's a critical constraint for "改了以后全改".

- **Liveness gate (不让改 while running)**: refuse rename/delete while the workmate is in use:
  (a) in-flight `mpd_workmate_spawn` in this process (track a live set of names with running spawns) — in-plugin, exact.
  (b) a live team member bound by name: needs team state. The agent-teams state lives in `.mpd/team` (stateDir override). There's no service. Reading team state files directly is a coupling. BUT the honest way: the workmate plugin may READ (never write) the team state dir to detect live teams on the same session? Hmm — the captain protocol forbids *me* (the agent) from inspecting .agent-teams state to revise plans; that's a captain rule, not a plugin rule. Still, coupling a plugin to another plugin's file format is fragile.

Alternative, cleaner and sanctioned: the **GUI/tool surface** can ask the agent-teams plugin via its **tools** — i.e. the workmate plugin calls `dsh.hasTool("agent_teams_status")` / `dsh.executeTool({name:"agent_teams_status"})` to get live team members, and refuses when a member name matches. That IS the sanctioned path exposed by the adapted API (§6: internal tool calls via the adapter). It's read-only and uses the public tool surface. That's elegant and reviewable.

Hmm, does `agent_teams_status` return all teams of all sessions and their members? The captain sees team mailbox etc. Status returns members + tasks for its own team... For a plugin executing the tool, which team context? Probably requires a session context. Risky. The implementation task must determine feasibility with evidence and choose: prefer adapter tool call; fallback to read-only scan of the team state dir (`.mpd/team/*/team.json`) for live (non-archived) teams.

Given the user's directive, the requirement is: **refuse while a live team has a member bound to that workmate; and when allowed, cascade all references** (dir key, meta.name, index key, note self-reference, `renamedFrom` continuity). For team-side references in ARCHIVED teams, "全改" can't be done without a sanctioned write API — so the honest scope: the liveness gate guarantees no LIVE team is affected; archived teams are historical records and must NOT be rewritten (they're records of what happened — rewriting history is wrong). I'll state that bound explicitly in the requirements: archived team records stay as-is (historical), and the plan documents it.

Hmm, but "改了以后全改" might also mean "after the rename, all the workmate's own artifacts/references must be updated" — which is exactly the cascade of self-references. I'll implement both readings that are safe: full self-reference cascade + liveness gate + explicit refusal semantics. And I'll surface this interpretation clearly to the user in the plan so they can correct it in review (the plan is staged for their approval — that IS the review point).

Also Q6 (name contract): I must decide. The user is Chinese; CJK names would sanitize to "". Options: (a) strict reject + document, (c) support Unicode dir names. Changing the key scheme touches members.js in BOTH plugins (byte-identical algorithm required) — that's a bigger change but genuinely valuable for a Chinese user ("给workmate改名" to something like "助理"?). Hmm. Risky: the agent-teams binding must stay byte-identical. Supporting unicode = modify sanitizeName in both plugins + tests. It's feasible but expands scope.

No** — better: include it as a decided design with an option flag?

Decision: implement strict-reject for rename (empty/invalid → clear error naming the reason, e.g. "name must contain [a-z0-9_-]"), AND support CJK by... hmm.

kind: requirements, round 1

acceptance:
- "Contract fixes the exact names/signatures of the new agent tools: mpd_workmate_rename and mpd_workmate_delete, their required/optional args (incl. the delete archive-vs-purge switch and the confirmation arg), return fields, and error messages."

Round 1: create T1 (requirements, Planner) and T2 (work dossier, Explorer).

Let me write substantial, precise descriptions.

T1:
subject: "Requirements contract + pinned wire protocol for workmate rename/delete"
kind: requirements, round 1
assignee: Planner
objective: "Turn the user-approved decisions into a binding, implementation-ready contract for workmate rename + delete: exact tool surface, exact HTTP wire protocol, refusal semantics, cascade list, archive layout, and error taxonomy — covering every edge case surfaced by the adversarial interrogation."
acceptance:
- "Contract fixes the exact names/signatures of the new agent tools: mpd_workmate_rename and mpd_workmate_delete, their required/optional args (incl. the delete archive-vs-purge switch and the confirmation arg), return fields, and error messages."
- "Contract fixes the exact HTTP wire protocol: path + method + request JSON + success/error body + status codes (405 wrong verb, 400 invalid JSON, 404 unknown name, 409/400 collision, cache-control: no-store) for every new route, byte-matching what the GUI task will call."
- "Contract pins the usage/liveness gate semantics: mutation is REFUSED while the workmate is in use (an in-flight spawn in this process, or a member of a live/non-archived team bound by name), naming the exact detection mechanism the implementation must use in this harness and its documented fallback."
- "Contract enumerates the complete cascade for rename: directory key, meta.name, index.json key, note.md self-reference, continuity metadata (renamedFrom/previousNames), updatedAt handling, and explicitly states which references are NOT rewritten (archived team records are historical and stay untouched)."
- "Contract pins delete semantics: default archive to ~/.mpd/workmate/.archive/<name>-<ISO>/ (hidden from list/match, restorable), purge for real removal, and the exact refusal when the instance is in use."
- "Contract pins name-safety invariants: ASCII-only key scheme ([a-z0-9_-]); any name whose sanitized form is empty/invalid is rejected BEFORE any filesystem call; no operation may ever resolve to, move, or recursively remove the library root; collisions (dir, file, or live workmate) are refused."
- "Contract carries the edge-case matrix with a decided outcome for each item (empty/invalid name, unknown name, double delete, half-created instance without meta.json, case-only rename, sanitization collision, symlinks, partial-failure atomicity, spawn/reflect race, service immediacy, readonly instances, headless profile without web routes)."
- "Verdict=pass with the contract text in the task output."
deliverables: ["requirements contract (task output text)", "edge-case matrix with decided outcomes (task output text)"]
nonGoals: ["Designing the implementation", "Editing any file (read-only role)"]
coverageOf: ["1. 可以给workmate改名", "2. 可以删除workmate"]

Also description with the user decisions verbatim.

T2:
subject: "Project traversal dossier: workmate system in the full bundle context"
kind: work
assignee: Explorer
description: the whole-repo traversal; deliverables: dossier text (task output).
No contract needed for kind=work, but let me still include deliverables/acceptance? For kind=work only subject required. I'll add description + deliverables.

Let me write these now. Keep descriptions detailed but not bloated.

Round 2: T3 (Senior Engineer, implementation, dep T1), T4 (Junior Engineer, implementation, dep T1), T5 (Deep Worker, implementation, no dep).

T3 details:
subject: "Implement workmate rename + delete in mpd-workmate-plugin (tools, service, routes, safety, tests)"
kind: implementation, round 1
assignee: Senior Engineer
dependencies: [T1]
objective: "Implement the rename and delete operations in packages/mpd-workmate-plugin exactly as the T1 contract pins them: new mpd_workmate_rename / mpd_workmate_delete tools, matching mpdWorkmate service methods, the new web routes, the usage/liveness refusal gate, the archive-first delete, full rename cascade, root-safety guards, and the workmate-side readonly deny-list correction — with unit tests and a rebuilt dist."
inScope: ["packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/", "evidence/workmate/rename-delete-core/"]
outOfScope: ["packages/mpd-roles-plugin/", "packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/", "packages/mpd-agent-teams-plugin/", "AGENTS.md", "docs/"]
acceptance: (list ~7)
 - "mpd_workmate_rename and mpd_workmate_delete are registered tools with the exact contract args/returns; the mpdWorkmate service exposes the matching methods and list/get/read reflect the mutation on the very next call (no caching)."
 - "After rename: old dir and old index key are gone; new dir basename === sanitizeName(meta.name) === the new index key; persona.md/memory.md/note.md content and caps, uses, lastTask and createdAt are preserved; note self-reference and continuity metadata updated; no re-instantiation and no uses bump."
 - "After delete (default archive): the instance is moved under ~/.mpd/workmate/.archive/<name>-<ISO>/ and disappears from list/match/service; with purge it is removed; the index key is dropped in both paths; no other workmate's bytes change."
 - "Usage/liveness gate: rename and delete are refused with a clear, actionable error while the workmate is in use (in-flight spawn in this process; a member bound by name in a live/non-archived team) using the mechanism T1 pinned; the refusal has zero side effects."
 - "Name safety: any invalid/empty-sanitized name is rejected before any filesystem call; a rename collision (existing dir/file/workmate) is refused; a rename to the same sanitized key is a defined no-op error; no operation can ever resolve to, move, or remove ~/.mpd/workmate itself (root-safety test present)."
 - "Web routes are registered per the T1 wire contract with the pinned verbs/status codes/cache-control, and the plugin still works tool-only in a headless profile with no web server service."
 - "The workmate-side READONLY_DENY no longer names tools this harness lacks (fix the readonly workmate spawn failure), pinned by a test."
 - "bun test packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/test/workmate.test.ts and bun run typecheck pass; dist/index.js is rebuilt; evidence written under evidence/workmate/rename-delete-core/<timestamp>/ with command output."
verify: 
 - "bun test packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/test/workmate.test.ts"
 - "bun run typecheck"
 - "cd packages/mpd-workmate-plugin && bun build src/index.ts --target node --format esm --outfile dist/index.js"
nonGoals: ["GUI/client changes (T4)", "roles-plugin deny list (T5)", "docs (T7)"]

Hmm: "The workmate-side READONLY_DENY no longer names tools this harness lacks" — good, and T5 does roles side.

Wait — is it safe/correct to just remove names? What ARE the correct tool names in this harness? Known: write, edit, mpd_hashline_edit, apply_patch? The harness has `write`, `edit`, `mpd_hashline_edit`. So deny should be ["write","edit","mpd_hashline_edit"] (+ maybe "mpd_comment_check"? no). The fix: drop the two unknown names. And also assert against the harness's known set — there's `dsh.hasTool(name)` at runtime; the plugin could filter the list dynamically by hasTool! That's a robust fix: `READONLY_DENY.filter(t => dsh.hasTool(t))`. Nice — I'll suggest that in the task as the preferred approach (filter at execute time so the list never goes stale). Good engineering. I'll mention it as a recommendation but let the implementer decide with the harness reality.

T4: GUI
subject: "Workmates sidebar tab: rename + delete controls (zh/en) and rebuilt client.js"
kind: implementation
assignee: Junior Engineer
dependencies: [T1]
objective: "Give the Workmates DSH-better-sidebar tab the human-facing half of the feature: rename and delete controls wired to the T1 wire contract, bilingual (zh/en) dictionary keys, safe confirmation for the destructive path, stale-selection handling, and a rebuilt packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/client.js."
inScope: ["packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/src/web-client.js", "packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/test/", "packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/client.js", "evidence/workmate/rename-delete-gui/"]
outOfScope: ["packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/", "packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/src/team-page.js", "AGENTS.md", "docs/"]
acceptance:
- "The workmate tab exposes rename (prefilled input) and delete (two-step arm-then-confirm, matching the archive-first semantics) for the selected workmate; both call ONLY the T1-pinned routes/methods/payloads."
- "Every new user-visible string exists in BOTH the zh and en dictionaries with identical key sets (zh remains the key-set source of truth)."
- "After a successful rename the view follows to the new name (or returns to the refreshed list) and after delete it returns to the list; no stale detail polling, no 404 loop, no second tab."
- "An in-use refusal from the host (liveness gate) surfaces as a readable message instead of an unhandled failure."
- "The tab remains sidebar-only (no floating fallback / footer toggle reintroduced) and the sidebar seam policy (ctx.inject(['betterSidebar'])) is unchanged."
- "node scripts/build-mpd-client.mjs succeeds and the committed client.js contains the new routes/markers; bun test packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/test/sidebar-tab.test.mjs (and the workmate tab assertions) pass; evidence under evidence/workmate/rename-delete-gui/<timestamp>/."
verify: ["node scripts/build-mpd-client.mjs", "bun test packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/test/sidebar-tab.test.mjs", "bun run typecheck"]

Hmm — `bun run typecheck` covers packages/*/src/**/*.ts only (client .js excluded). Fine, harmless but let me keep only relevant ones. Also client-harness.mjs test may need updating. Let me include "bun test packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/test".

T5: readonly deny fix
subject: "Fix the read-only deny lists so readonly spawn works on the real harness"
kind: implementation
assignee: Deep Worker
dependencies: [] (independent)
objective: "Fix the live defect that read-only spawns fail on this harness: the deny lists name global tools that do not exist (str_replace_editor, apply_patch) and the harness rejects the whole restriction call, so mpd_role_spawn for read-only roster roles (and readonly workmate spawn on the workmate side, owned by T3) never applies. Prove the fix against the REAL dsh tool registry, not a stub."
inScope: ["packages/mpd-roles-plugin/", "skills/dsh-qa/scripts/", "evidence/workmate/roles-readonly/"]
outOfScope: ["packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/", "packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/", "AGENTS.md", "docs/"]
acceptance:
- "packages/mpd-roles-plugin READONLY_DENY no longer contains any global tool name this harness does not register; the list is either corrected or filtered against the live tool registry so it can never go stale again."
- "A regression test proves the restriction list names only tools that exist in the real harness (not a stub), and that a read-only role spawn no longer fails with the 'names unknown global tools' error."
- "A dsh-qa case (script + --self-test + SKILL.md case-table row) boots the real dsh in an isolated DSH_HOME/HOME and demonstrates the read-only spawn path succeeds; it never touches the real ~/.dsh or real HOME."
- "The QA self-test sweep (bun run test:qa) still passes."
- "Evidence under evidence/workmate/roles-readonly/<timestamp>/ with the failing-before / passing-after command output."
verify: ["bun test packages/mpd-roles-plugin/test", "bun run test:qa", "bun run typecheck"]
nonGoals: ["The workmate-side deny line (T3)", "Changing the roster, its personas or its model routes", "Widening what read-only roles may write"]

Hmm: is verifying "a read-only role spawn no longer fails" possible without an LLM? mpd_role_spawn spawns a subagent → needs a live session/LLM. The QA case with real dsh boot + LLM is the live path (credentials copied into sandbox). The repo's QA skill supports live cases. It might be expensive but it's the honest proof. Alternatively, prove at the API level: the harness's `tools.restrict` acceptance. Could a live case call the tool directly without an LLM? The mpd-qa-roles-probe package does "mpd preset resolve + mpdRoles roster" — there's a QA probe package! `packages/mpd-qa-roles-probe`. Maybe the QA path can boot a headless session with a scripted prompt... Let me not over-specify: acceptance says "boots the real dsh in an isolated DSH_HOME/HOME and demonstrates the read-only spawn path succeeds" — the implementer will find the cheapest real proof (maybe calling restrict via the harness API in a probe session). Good.

Round 3:
T6 verification — assignee Reviewer? Hmm, wait: I assigned RV1 (review of T3) to Architect, RV2 (T4) to Plan Reviewer, RV3 (T5) to Senior Engineer, T6 verification to Reviewer, T7 docs to Lead, T8 integration to Lead.

T6:
subject: "Independent verification of rename/delete end-to-end and the full gate sweep"
kind: verification
assignee: Reviewer
dependencies: [T3, T4, T5]
objective: "Independently verify the rename/delete feature and the readonly fix against the real harness and the real gates — not against the implementers' summaries: run every gate, exercise the lifecycle in a sandbox HOME (rename preserves identity, delete archives, purge removes, in-use refusal fires, invalid/empty names are rejected with zero side effects and never touch the library root), boot the bundle in an isolated DSH_HOME, and capture evidence on disk."
acceptance:
- "Every gate command from AGENTS.md §4 is run and its real output recorded: bun test packages, bun run typecheck, bun run test:qa, node scripts/verify-vendor.mjs, and a dsh --profile headless --dump-config boot in an isolated DSH_HOME."
- "A real sandbox-HOME exercise demonstrates: rename keeps persona/memory/note/uses/createdAt byte-identical and frees the old key; delete archives by default (restorable under .archive/) and purges on demand; list/match/service views agree with the filesystem immediately after each mutation."
- "Negative cases demonstrably pass: empty/CJK/punctuation-only name rejected before any filesystem call (library root untouched), unknown name errors with zero side effects, double delete errors, rename collision refused, rename/delete refused while the workmate is in use."
- "The web routes answer per the T1 contract (real boot: correct status codes for success/invalid/unknown/wrong-verb), and the readonly spawn fix is demonstrated against the real harness."
- "Every command result is recorded in commandsRun with exit codes and evidence; results.json/output.log written under evidence/workmate/rename-delete-verify/<timestamp>/; the real HOME and real ~/.dsh are never touched (sandbox asserted)."
verify: ["bun test packages", "bun run typecheck", "bun run test:qa", "node scripts/verify-vendor.mjs"]
inScope: ["evidence/workmate/rename-delete-verify/"]
Hmm — a verification task's inScope: only evidence. Fine.
outOfScope: ["packages/** (verification must not fix; failures go back as findings)"]
nonGoals: ["Fixing anything yourself", "Approving the implementation"]

RV1 review of T3 → Architect:
subject: "Review: core rename/delete implementation (safety, identity, atomicity, races)"
kind: review, round 1, reviewedTaskId T3
assignee: Architect
objective: "Adversarially review the T3 implementation against the T1 contract on the points where a bug is expensive: root-safety, name sanitization, identity preservation, atomicity/partial failure, index consistency, spawn/reflect races, service immediacy, and the readonly deny correction — judging the LATEST implementation state, not the implementer's summary."
acceptance:
- "Each T1 acceptance criterion is checked against the code and evidence with pass/fail and a concrete citation (file/line or command output)."
- "The review explicitly attempts to falsify the invariants: I1 (name↔dir↔index bijection + root safety), I2 (rename is identity-preserving, never a re-instantiation), I3 (delete complete and all-or-nothing), I4 (deterministic cross-module binding outcome) — reporting any counterexample found."
- "Race/failure analysis covers: reflect after rename (old-dir resurrection), reflect/delete ordering, partial failure between the directory move and the metadata write, and the in-flight spawn liveness gate."
- "Verdict is pass only with zero unresolved blocker/high findings; otherwise fail with structured findings (id/severity/problem/requiredFix) that name the exact file and the required fix."
inScope: [] hmm, review tasks don't need inScope. Only implementation/repair require inScope. Right: "implementation/repair also need inScope and verify". So reviews need objective + acceptance only.

RV2 review of T4 → Plan Reviewer:
subject: "Review: Workmates tab rename/delete UI, locale keys and rebuilt client"
kind: review, round 1, reviewedTaskId T4
objective: "Review the T4 GUI work as a UI/UX and contract-conformance reviewer: does the tab actually let a human rename and safely delete a workmate, does every string exist in both zh and en with identical key sets, do the calls match the T1 wire contract exactly, and are the destructive path, refusal messaging and stale-selection handling sound?"
acceptance:
- "Wire-contract conformance is verified call-by-call (path/method/payload/response handling) against T1 — any drift is a finding."
- "Every new visible string is present in both dictionaries with identical key sets; a missing zh or en key is at least a high finding."
- "The destructive flow is human-safe: explicit confirmation, archive-first wording that matches the host semantics, no single-click irreversible action, and a readable message on an in-use refusal."
- "The sidebar design constraints hold: sidebar-only tab (no floating fallback / footer toggle), single:true, no stale detail polling or 404 loop after a mutation, and client.js is rebuilt so the shipped bundle contains the new UI."
- "Verdict is pass only with zero unresolved blocker/high findings; otherwise fail with structured findings naming the file and the required fix."

RV3 review of T5 → Senior Engineer:
subject: "Review: read-only deny-list defect fix and its real-harness proof"
kind: review, round 1, reviewedTaskId T5
objective: "Review the T5 fix on correctness of the diagnosis and strength of the proof: does the deny list now name only tools this harness registers, is the mechanism robust rather than a one-off literal patch, does the regression actually exercise the real harness (not a stub), and did the fix avoid widening read-only authority?"
acceptance:
- "The root cause is confirmed against the harness's real tool registry and the fix is shown to remove it (before/after evidence cited)."
- "The regression/QA case is evaluated for real-harness fidelity: it must fail on the pre-fix code or on the original deny list, and pass after — a stub-only assertion is a finding."
- "Read-only authority is verified not to have widened: the roles remain unable to write (no write/edit/apply_patch-style tool becomes available)."
- "Verdict is pass only with zero unresolved blocker/high findings; otherwise fail with structured findings naming the file and the required fix."

Round 4:
T7 docs/sync → Lead, kind implementation, deps [T3, T4, T5]:
subject: "Bilingual docs + QA surface sync for workmate rename/delete"
objective: "Sync every human-facing and agent-facing surface with the shipped feature: the package README pair, the user guide pair, AGENTS.md (workmate tool list, glossary, troubleshooting), and the QA scripts that assert the workmate route literals — both language versions in the same change, and the QA assertions extended to the new routes."
inScope: ["packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/README.md", "packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/README.zh-CN.md", "AGENTS.md", "docs/user-guide.md", "docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md", "skills/dsh-qa/scripts/workmate-library.mjs", "skills/dsh-qa/scripts/web-client-adapt.mjs", "skills/dsh-qa/SKILL.md", "evidence/workmate/rename-delete-docs/"]
outOfScope: ["packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/src/", "packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/src/", "packages/mpd-roles-plugin/", "the readonly-spawn QA case and its SKILL.md row (T5)"]
acceptance:
- "packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/README.md and README.zh-CN.md both document the new tools/routes/semantics (archive-first delete, in-use refusal, ASCII naming) with the language switch link directly under each title; neither version is left stale."
- "docs/user-guide.md and docs/user-guide.zh-CN.md are updated in the same change wherever the workmate workflow is described, keeping the switch links intact."
- "AGENTS.md carries the new tool names in the workmate tool list, updates the workmate glossary entry, and adds troubleshooting rows for the rename/delete failure modes (in-use refusal, archived instance restore, invalid/CJK name rejection)."
- "The QA scripts assert the new routes/routes-list so the shipped surface is pinned by test:qa (workmate-library.mjs and web-client-adapt.mjs updated, their --self-test still passes, and SKILL.md's case table matches reality)."
- "Docs claim nothing the code does not do: every documented tool name, route, flag and status code is verified against the shipped sources."
verify: ["bun run test:qa", "bun test packages/mpd-bundle-plugin/test", "bun run typecheck"]

T8 integration → Lead, kind integration, round 1, deps [T6, RV1, RV2, RV3, T7, T2]:
subject: "Integrate and report: rename/delete feature, defect fix, docs and evidence as one coherent change"
objective: "Integrate the verified, reviewed work into one coherent change on disk and report it honestly: reconcile docs against the shipped code and the T2 dossier, persist the T1 contract and T2 dossier into the evidence tree, re-run the final gate sweep on the integrated tree, and summarize what changed, what was verified, and what remains open."
acceptance:
- "The T1 requirements contract and the T2 project-traversal dossier are persisted on disk under evidence/workmate/rename-delete-integration/<timestamp>/ (read-only members delivered them as text)."
- "A code↔docs consistency pass confirms every tool name, route, flag, status code and refusal semantic documented in AGENTS.md/READMEs/user guide matches the shipped sources; any drift is fixed or reported as an open finding."
- "The final integrated tree passes the gate sweep (bun test packages, bun run typecheck, bun run test:qa, node scripts/verify-vendor.mjs) with the real output recorded."
- "The delivery report states: changed files, the exact user decisions implemented (archive-first delete, in-use refusal + full library-owned cascade, readonly defect fixed, tools+GUI surface, ASCII-only naming), what is explicitly NOT rewritten (archived team records), verification evidence paths, and any residual risk or follow-up."
- "No quality gate is left failed and no review finding from RV1/RV2/RV3 is left unresolved at integration time."
inScope: ["evidence/workmate/rename-delete-integration/"]
Hmm, integration may need to fix docs drift → outOfScope packages. Let me give it inScope: docs paths too: ["AGENTS.md", "docs/", "packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/README.md", "packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/README.zh-CN.md", "evidence/workmate/rename-delete-integration/"]. Good.

That's 11 tasks: T1..T8 + RV1..RV3 = 11. Reasonable for a "small-to-medium" task with quality mode. Hmm, "smallest useful task graph" — 11 tasks with 11 members. It's proportional to a 3-surface implementation with bilingual docs + a defect fix. OK.

Let me now create tasks. Round 1: T1, T2.

Note: assignee names must match member names: "Planner", "Explorer", "Senior Engineer", "Junior Engineer", "Deep Worker", "Reviewer", "Architect", "Plan Reviewer", "Lead".

Let me write the calls. I'll do T1 and T2 in one block.
Now I'll stage the task DAG on the already-staged `MPD Default` team (profile `mpd`), encoding your five decisions.

Read the T1 contract first, then the actual code in packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/src/index.ts, the tests and the evidence — and treat the implementer's summary as a claim to be checked, not as fact.

Specific things to attack:
- sanitizeName as the single key algorithm: can any input reach a filesystem call before validation? What exactly happens for an empty sanitized name, a CJK name, a punctuation-only name, a name differing only by case, and a name colliding after sanitization?
- rename identity: is the evolved instance really moved rather than recreated? Are persona/memory/note content, the caps, uses, lastTask and createdAt preserved? Is the note self-reference and the continuity metadata consistent with the new name?
- delete: archive-first behaviour, hidden-from-list/match, restorability, purge, index-key removal, and all-or-nothing failure behaviour.
- the in-use gate: does it really prevent the spawn/reflect race, or does it only shift the window? Is the chosen detection mechanism sound in this harness, and does it avoid writing to another plugin's state?
- index.json: it has no reader today — judge whether the rename/delete handling leaves it consistent and whether the contract's treatment of it is defensible.
- the workmate-side READONLY_DENY correction (part of t3): does it actually fix readonly spawn, and does it keep read-only authority intact?

data.arguments:
{"acceptance": ["Every AGENTS.md §4 gate is run on the integrated tree with real output recorded: bun test packages, bun run typecheck, bun run test:qa, node scripts/verify-vendor.mjs, and a `dsh --profile headless --dump-config` boot in an isolated DSH_HOME.", "A real sandbox-HOME lifecycle exercise demonstrates, from the outside (tools/service/routes, not by reading the implementer's code): rename preserves persona/memory/note/uses/createdAt and frees the old key; delete archives by default and the instance is restorable from .archive/; purge removes it; list/match/service views agree with the filesystem immediately after every mutation.", "Negative cases demonstrably behave: invalid/empty/CJK/punctuation-only names are rejected before any filesystem call with the library root untouched; unknown names error with zero side effects; a repeated delete errors; a rename collision is refused; a rename or delete is refused while the workmate is in use.", "The new web routes answer per the T1 contract on a real boot (correct status codes for success, invalid body, unknown name, wrong verb) and the read-only spawn path is demonstrated to work against the real harness.", "Every command result is recorded in commandsRun with exit codes and evidence, and results.json/output.log are written under evidence/workmate/rename-delete-verify/<timestamp>/.", "The real HOME and the real ~/.dsh are never touched (the sandbox path is asserted in the evidence)."], "assignee": "Reviewer", "dependencies": ["t3", "t4", "t5"], "description": "Verify the delivered feature independently. Do not trust the implementers' summaries: reproduce from the real artifacts (source, built dist, real dsh boot, sandboxed filesystem) and treat any mismatch between a claim and the observed behaviour as a finding you report — you do not fix code yourself.

Method that fits this repo: follow the dsh-qa discipline (skills/dsh-qa) — an isolated DSH_HOME and HOME per run, credentials copied once into the sandbox, sandbox paths asserted, evidence written under evidence/<domain>/<slug>/<timestamp>/{result.json,output.log}, and long-lived MCP children run with stdio to files rather than pipes. The workmate library lives under $HOME, so every lifecycle exercise MUST run with HOME pointing at a sandbox and the evidence must show it.

Pay particular attention to the cases where a naive implementation is quietly wrong: a name that sanitizes to an empty string (wmDir("") is the library root itself), a rename that loses evolved memory or bumps uses, a delete that leaves the index stale or removes only part of the instance, a mutation racing an in-flight spawn, and a GUI-visible route that answers 200 on an unknown name.

If something fails, report it as a failed verification with the exact command, exit code and output — the scheduler turns that into a repair loop. Do not edit implementation files.", "inScope": ["evidence/workmate/rename-delete-verify/"], "nonGoals": ["Fixing anything yourself", "Approving the implementation", "Editing package sources, docs or QA scripts"], "objective": "Independently verify the shipped rename/delete feature and the read-only deny fix against the REAL harness and the REAL gates: run every gate, exercise the full lifecycle and its negative cases with HOME pointed at a sandbox, boot the bundle in an isolated DSH_HOME, confirm the web routes and the read-only spawn path behave as contracted, and leave reproducible evidence on disk.", "outOfScope": ["packages/", "AGENTS.md", "docs/", "skills/dsh-qa/scripts/"], "round": 1, "subject": "Independent verification: rename/delete end-to-end, negative cases, full gate sweep", "verify": ["bun test packages", "bun run typecheck", "bun run test:qa", "node scripts/verify-vendor.mjs"]}

t10: docs — kind implementation with inScope+verify. Wait, docs is not really "implementation" but the kind requires inScope + verify; I have both. Alternatively kind=work with explicit acceptance in description. Hmm: if I use kind=implementation, the system might expect a review. Not required. But quality-wise, a doc task as "implementation" with verify commands is fine and gives the gate a contract.

Actually let me use kind=work for docs to keep semantics honest (docs aren't code implementation) but still list acceptance in the description. Hmm — but then there's no formal acceptance field. The DAG protocol says quality kinds need contracts; `work` needs only a subject. Given quality mode, I prefer the contract to exist. I'll use kind=implementation since the task does change shipped files (docs + QA scripts) and has real verify commands. That's defensible.

t11 integration: kind=integration with objective+acceptance. deps: t6, t7, t8, t9, t10, t2.

Hmm — integration depends on t9 (review of t5, owned by Senior Engineer). Note t9's assignee Senior Engineer also owns t3. That's fine.

Wait, there's a scheduling nuance: RV3 (t9) depends on t5, and is assigned to Senior Engineer who owns t3. If t5 finishes while t3 is still running, t9 sits pending until t3 completes. Fine.

Another nuance: t6 (verification, Reviewer) depends on t3, t4, t5. And t10 (docs, Lead) depends on t3, t4, t5. Parallel — but both may touch different files: t6 only writes evidence; t10 writes docs + skills/dsh-qa/scripts/{workmate-library,web-client-adapt}.mjs + SKILL.md. T5 (Deep Worker) also touches skills/dsh-qa/scripts (new case) + SKILL.md. t10 depends on t5 so ordering is safe (t5 completes first). But note t6 runs `bun run test:qa` (the self-test sweep over skills/dsh-qa/scripts/*.mjs) while t10 edits those scripts — if t10 edits while t6 runs the sweep, the result could be inconsistent. Both run in parallel after t3/t4/t5.

Hmm. That's a real (if small) hazard. Options: make t6 depend on t10 too, or make t10 depend on t6. Better: t6 (verification) should verify the FINAL tree, including the docs/QA-script sync. But docs don't affect code behavior. However `test:qa` sweeps the QA scripts — which t10 modifies. So t6's sweep could fail on t10's in-flight edits.

Cleanest: t10 (docs/sync) depends on t5 (done) and runs in parallel; t6 depends on t10 as well → verification runs on the synced tree. But then verification waits for docs → serializes the critical path a lot (docs after all impl, then verification, then integration).

Alternative: t10 (docs) depends on t6, t3, t4, t5 → docs after verification. Then t11 integration depends on t10 + reviews. That's a clean sequence: impl (parallel) → verify + reviews (parallel) → docs/sync → integration. And the "verification of the final tree" isn't strictly true for docs, but docs are checked by integration's consistency pass (t11's acceptance includes code↔docs consistency). And t10 itself runs `bun run test:qa` in its verify.

Hmm, but that makes verification not cover the QA script changes t10 makes. t10's own verify covers test:qa. Acceptable: t11 integration re-runs the gate sweep on the integrated tree (acceptance includes final gate sweep with real output). Good — the final tree IS gate-swept by t11.

Decision: t10 deps = [t3, t4, t5, t6] — docs after the verified state (docs must describe what was verified). Then t11 deps = [t6, t7, t8, t9, t10, t2].

Oops — I accidentally wrote "packages/mpd-social-plugin/" in outOfScope (a hallucinated package name). Harmless (it just lists a non-existent path as out of scope), but let me fix it with agent_teams_edit_plan? Editing a staged plan is allowed via agent_teams_edit_plan (update_task). Since the team is staged, I can update the task. Let me do it as part of a final edit_plan batch, or just leave it? It's a cosmetic error but sloppy; an outOfScope entry naming a non-existent package is confusing in the plan the user reads. Let me fix it in one edit_plan operation... Actually for a staged team, `agent_teams_create_task` created real tasks; edit_plan ops include update_task with task_id. Does update_task support replacing outOfScope? The operation fields: action, task_id, subject, description, assignee, dependencies... There's no outOfScope field in the edit_plan schema! Fields: action, assignee, dependencies, description, member_name, provider, model, reasoning_effort, role, subject, task_id, execution_prompt. So no outOfScope replacement. I could remove and recreate the task, but that's churn and risks id changes.

Alternatively leave it — it's harmless. Actually, cleanest: it's a minor cosmetic inconsistency in a field the user may read. I'll leave it and mention nothing? Hmm, better to keep the plan clean. I could recreate t10 with the corrected outOfScope: remove_task t10 then add_task (new id t12) — but dependencies of t11 (which I haven't created yet) point to t10's id... I haven't created t11 yet! So I can: remove t10, add t10-corrected as a new task, then create t11 with the new id.

Hmm, is that worth it? The plan quality matters. `outOfScope` listing a non-existent package could confuse an implementer ("is there a social plugin?"). Small confusion risk. Let me just do the clean thing: use edit_plan with remove_task + add_task (new id) and then create t11 referencing the new id.

Actually wait — simpler alternative: keep t10 and simply not worry; when creating t11 I'll reference t10. The outOfScope entry is harmless noise but the plan is what the user reviews; a bogus path is a credibility ding. I'll fix it.

Plan: agent_teams_edit_plan([{action:"remove_task", task_id:"t10"}, {action:"add_task", subject:...}]) — but add_task in edit_plan: does it support kind/acceptance/deliverables/inScope/verify/objective/round? The schema for edit_plan operations is limited: action, subject, description, assignee, dependencies, ... no kind/objective/inScope. So an add_task via edit_plan can't carry a contract → can't create a quality task there. It would create a legacy `work` task without the contract. Not good.

So: remove t10 via edit_plan, then recreate it properly via agent_teams_create_task (full contract). Let me do that: two calls — edit_plan(remove t10) then create_task. But edit_plan on a staged plan is allowed now (it's the sanctioned revision path). Hmm, the captain protocol says edit_plan is used when the user returns to chat to request changes. Using it now for a self-correction is fine mechanically.

Honestly, the simplest robust option: leave t10 as is and move on — the cost/benefit favors momentum. But a bogus package path in the approved plan is exactly the kind of sloppiness a reviewer would flag...

Let me weigh once more: is outOfScope with a non-existent path harmful during execution? No: it just means "don't touch this", and nobody will. It's cosmetic. But it's also visible in the Web plan UI.

Decision: fix it via remove+recreate (cheap, 2 calls, no dependencies broken since t11 doesn't exist yet). Actually — careful: does remove_task work on a staged plan whose task was just created? Should be fine.

Hmm, one risk: the id may be reused (t10) or incremented (t11). If the new one gets a different id, I must use it in t11's deps. Fine.

Reproduction the captain already confirmed:

  mpd_role_spawn(role=...) for every READ-ONLY roster role fails immediately with:
  Error: tools.restrict() names unknown global tools "str_replace_editor", "apply_patch";
  known global tools: agent_teams_add_member, agent_teams_approve, ... (the harness's full list).

The deny list lives at packages/mpd-roles-plugin/src/index.ts (READONLY_DENY, ~line 23-27, used at ~line 123 as `toolFilter: { deny: READONLY_DENY }` when spec.readonly). Two of the denied names come from a different agent harness and do not exist here, and this harness rejects the WHOLE restriction call when any name is unknown, so the read-only discipline silently became 'no spawn at all'. The existing unit tests only assert the deny array's construction against a stub adapter, so they never caught it. A sibling line exists in mpd-workmate-plugin (line 30) but it belongs to the core implementation task, NOT to you — do not touch it.

2. Quiet the standby loop: the members are turning repeatedly and reporting nothing. This will keep happening as long as the team loop is "running" but nothing is approved. I should not spam them; the best action is to wait for user approval. But the repeated standby turns are wasteful.

But careful about my own constraints: "Do not start a replacement server unless the user asks; if one is needed, use a managed background job and verify its exact URL." Booting an isolated QA instance on a scratch port for a screenshot is a QA activity, not a replacement for the user's GUI. It's within the repo's QA discipline (dsh-qa boots isolated profiles). The user's GUI at 127.0.0.1:3080 remains untouched. That's acceptable — but it's also substantial extra scope.

Is the juice worth the squeeze? The user's feature is a GUI change ("可以给workmate改名/删除" with the sidebar tab). Rendered verification would be genuinely valuable — the repo has a history of sidebar breakage (the troubleshooting table). And a Vision Analyst is on the roster; the visual-qa skill exists.

Risk: if the browser tooling turns out unusable, the task fails → repair loop noise. I can mitigate by scoping acceptance to be honest: "verify the rendered UI; if the sandbox cannot run a real browser, report the exact blocker as a finding instead of fabricating pixel evidence, and fall back to a rendered-DOM/markup-level visual review with explicit confidence labels". Hmm. Better: let me actually verify playwright availability NOW (cheap, decisive), then decide.

- global npm root / bun global for playwright
- `~/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1228/chrome-linux/chrome` exists?
- any `playwright-core` inside ~/.nvm/.../lib/node_modules or in the DSH checkout's node_modules (the harness may bundle playwright for web tests!)

If a usable chromium binary + a driver exist, the task is executable.

b. Also: should I stop the standby churn? I can't "pause" the loop except by asking the user to approve/discard, or by sending a single guidance message to the standby members telling them to hold. Actually the messages say they finished their turns (idle). The loop "running" state apparently re-turns members periodically? That could keep spinning. One efficient action: send ONE message to the team? There's no broadcast; but I could message each standby member — that's 8 messages of noise and would actually START turns for them (send_message to idle starts a turn!) — the opposite of what I want.

So: do NOT message idle members (it would wake them). Their turns seem to be driven by the loop; they'll settle. The protocol says don't require reports from members with no assigned work.

Hmm, but they keep turning. Notice: the pattern seems to be that members spawn once and each took one turn (the loop "running" during staging appears to have spawned+run standby turns). Vision Analyst's subagent finished/failed. Maybe this settles now.

The right captain move: reply to the Vision Analyst's *request* by deciding — the message from Vision Analyst came via the mailbox, but replying with send_message would start a turn for it. If I create a task for it, the task is the answer (it will be assigned when the plan runs). Since the plan is staged, adding a task is a plan edit, not a spawn. Good: no wake-up.

Let me check playwright availability, then decide on adding the visual task.

Let me also reconsider: is adding the visual QA task scope creep that the user didn't ask for? The user asked to traverse the project and optimize the workmate system with rename + delete. Verifying the GUI visually is part of delivering a GUI feature well. Given the roster includes a Vision Analyst asking for work and the repo has `visual-qa` skill + playwright browser cache, it's a reasonable, bounded addition. But plan bloat is a real cost: the user must review it.

Middle ground: add ONE visual-verification task (kind=verification, Vision Analyst, deps t16 + t22?) — placed after t16 so the UI exists, and it can run in parallel with t18's gate sweep. Then t23 integration depends on it too.

Hmm, but if t23 depends on it and it fails for environmental reasons, integration blocks. Let me first check playwright. Decide after.

A wave of teammates checked in — all correctly idle, none claiming blocked work. The Vision Analyst's offer is legitimate though: a GUI change deserves rendered verification. Let me check whether this sandbox can actually drive a browser before amending the plan.

Registrations are reversible effects via ctx.effect()/ctx.on().

- Tool registration: ctx.tools.register(defineTool({name, description, parameters, output:{schema,render}, execute})). ToolDefinition = ToolSchema + output + execute + finalizeContent + presentCall/presentResult. Built-in tools in packages: dsh-tool-bash, dsh-tool-fs (read/edit/write), dsh-tool-fs-search (glob/grep via ripgrep), dsh-tool-subagent, dsh-tool-goal (create_goal/get_goal/update_goal), dsh-tool-lsp. Third-party tools compose via ctx.tools.register ...

Hmm, actually, hold on. Let me reconsider messaging the Junior Engineer: it already knows (it raised the hazard and did the analysis). Its message asked me to "pin the baseline". A reply IS the answer to a direct request — appropriate. Yes.

Skip — but the user should know (in my summary).
   Hmm, but the Vision Analyst explicitly offered and asked. Leaving a direct offer unanswered is slightly impolite but the cost/benefit favors silence; a running team's members shouldn't be woken for "no work". Actually... there's a subtle consideration: on delivery, t23 might want the visual QA. Not applicable (no browser).
   Decision: skip messaging Vision Analyst; report the rationale to the user.
2. Researcher: offered 3 lanes; I decided none is needed (lane 2 duplicates t2, lane 3 duplicates t19, lane 1 is nice-to-have that would arrive too late to inform t1/t15). Skip messaging (same cost logic). Report to the user.
   Hmm, is there a case for lane 1 as a genuinely additive independent task? Consider: the contract t1 will pin semantics for tombstones/aliases — external prior art COULD change the design (e.g. "keep a tombstone so old names can't be silently reused"). But the user already decided: archive-first delete, in-use refusal, full cascade. A tombstone-on-rename question remains open (momus raised it as Q5: old name freed immediately → potential identity swap). Planner's t1 contract should decide it. If I had a Researcher, it could... eh. The contract will decide; a later user decision can adjust. Keep it lean. Skip.

The guidance persists in their context? Members have their own session; the message lands in their mailbox and is delivered as a turn. When the scheduler later wakes them, do they still see the earlier mail? Their session is durable ("durable continuable member"), so yes, prior turns persist in their context. Good — guidance survives.

Let me send the messages and then write this up. Keep the final message tight — the user's hands are on the approve button, not on a wall of text.

Actually, I should also set up monitoring: the loop will notify me on progress. I'll end the turn after messaging.

Let me write the three messages concisely.

## B. Identity + name rules

- The **instance key IS the directory name** (`~/.mpd/workmate/<key>/`). `meta.name` is a display mirror:
  repaired on the next write, never used for path resolution. This is what makes an interrupted rename harmless.
- Name validation applies to **both** arguments of rename and to delete's name:
  accept iff `raw === sanitizeName(raw) && raw !== ""` (and length <= 255). This is a superset of every existing
  key, so no instance becomes un-addressable, while `"Alice"`, CJK, `"a/b"`, `".."`, `".archive"` are all
  rejected before any fs call.
- **`wmDir("")` currently resolves to the LIBRARY ROOT** — the implementation must guard it so the root can never
  be moved, renamed or removed.
- Collisions: renaming onto an existing directory/file/workmate is refused. Renaming to the same key is a defined
  outcome (rejected, no side effect). Case-only rename is rejected (it sanitizes to the same key).

## C. Agent tools (exact surface)

- `mpd_workmate_rename { name, new_name }`
- `mpd_workmate_delete { name, purge?, confirm? }` — `purge: true` requires `confirm === name`, otherwise refused.
- `mpdWorkmate` service gains exactly `rename(...)` and `delete(...)`; `list` / `get` / `read` must reflect the
  mutation on the very next call (no caching): `get(oldKey)` -> null, `get(newKey)` -> full detail.

## D. HTTP wire protocol (exact)

`POST /plugins/mpd-workmate/rename` and `POST /plugins/mpd-workmate/delete`, JSON bodies, plus the existing
`GET /list`, `GET /roster`, `GET /get?name=` and `POST /init` unchanged. Every response:
`content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8`, `cache-control: no-store`.

| Condition | Status | Body |
|---|---|---|
| success (rename) | 200 | `{ ok: true, name: <newKey>, from: <oldKey>, ... }` |
| success (delete, archive) | 200 | `{ ok: true, name, archived: "<path>", purged: false }` |
| success (delete, purge) | 200 | `{ ok: true, name, archived: null, purged: true }` |
| wrong verb | 405 | `allow: POST` header, empty body |
| invalid JSON body | 400 | `{ error }` |
| invalid / non-ASCII / empty name | 400 | `{ error, reason: "invalid-name" }` |
| unknown workmate (also a repeat delete) | 404 | `{ error, reason: "unknown" }` |
| rename target already exists | 409 | `{ error, reason: "collision" }` |
| refused because the workmate is in use | 409 | `{ error, reason: "in-use", blocking: [{ teamId, member }] }` |
| purge without `confirm === name` | 400 | `{ error, reason: "confirm-required" }` |

Route registration stays lazy behind the existing `webRegistered` guard, so a headless profile works tool-only.
Do NOT leak absolute `$HOME` paths in error bodies (the existing `init` returning `path` is a deliberate
exception, not a precedent).

- (a) an in-process `Map<key, count>` incremented/decremented around `dsh.spawnAgent` in `mpd_workmate_spawn`;
- (b) a read-only scan of **direct children** of `<workspace>/.mpd/team/<teamId>/team.json`
  (archived teams live under `.mpd/team/archive/**`, excluded by construction), matching
  `workmateKey(member.name)`.
- **Reading that state is permitted; WRITING to `.mpd/team` is forbidden.** Fail-open on any read error.

  it race-free in-process — no lock file needed.

  non-archived team records under `.mpd/team/` whose members are named Planner/Researcher/Architect…; without the
  names the refusal is not actionable.

  `oracle-1` to `architect`) is refused while such a team record exists. Archiving those teams (AgentTeams panel)
  removes the block.

## F. Rename cascade (complete) and delete semantics

Rename updates: directory key, `meta.name`, the `index.json` key, the `note.md` self-reference
(`autoNote` writes `<baseName>-based workmate "<name>".`), and a continuity field (`renamedFrom` / previous names).
It does **not** re-copy the base, does not reset memory, does not bump `uses`; it does update `updatedAt`.
Persona/memory/note content, caps, `uses`, `lastTask` and `createdAt` are preserved byte-for-byte.
Explicitly NOT rewritten: archived team records (historical).

Delete: archive path `~/.mpd/workmate/.archive/<key>-<compactUtcStamp>/` (colons stripped for Windows
portability); the instance disappears from `list`/`match`/service immediately; the index key is dropped in both
the archive and purge paths; no other workmate's bytes change; a failed delete never leaves a partially removed
instance.

## G. Read-only deny list (CAPTAIN-CORRECTED — overrides the original t1 finding)

The original t1 claimed `apply_patch` was the only dead name and that `str_replace_editor` must be kept.
That is **wrong**, verified live twice by the captain with `mpd_role_spawn`:

```
Error: tools.restrict() names unknown global tools "str_replace_editor", "apply_patch";
known global tools: … bash … edit … mpd_hashline_edit … read … write
```

- The harness validates the whole list and reports BOTH names as unknown.
- The `known global tools` enumeration IS the live registry of this profile: it contains `write`, `edit`,
  `mpd_hashline_edit` and **neither** `str_replace_editor` nor `apply_patch`.
- An installed `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-str-replace-editor` package and a `dsh-base` patch row exist, but that row is
  not composed into this profile — a patch row is not proof of runtime registration.

Therefore **both** names must be removed from every `READONLY_DENY`
(`packages/mpd-roles-plugin/src/index.ts` and `packages/mpd-workmate-plugin/src/index.ts`), leaving exactly
`["write","edit","mpd_hashline_edit"]`. Keeping either dead name leaves every read-only spawn failing with the
identical error.

**Forbidden fix:** do NOT filter the list with `dsh.hasTool` — it reads the GLOBAL tool view only, so
`write`/`edit`/`bash` (registered on the agent plane by the mpd preset) answer false and filtering would silently
drop them, leaving read-only children un-guarded. Only the genuinely optional MCP names
(`mcp__ast_grep__rewrite|scan`, `mcp__lsp__rename`) may be resolved that way.

## H. Edge-case matrix (each row needs a decided outcome; all must be covered by tests)

empty/invalid/CJK/punctuation-only name · unknown name · repeat delete (404) · half-created instance without
`meta.json` · case-only rename · sanitization collision ("Alice Cooper" vs "alice-cooper") · symlinked instance
dir (refused, not resolved) · partial failure between directory move and metadata write · spawn/reflect racing a
rename (old-dir resurrection) · reflect after delete · `list`/`get`/`read` immediacy · readonly instance as the
target of a mutation · headless profile with no `webServer` · GUI stale selection after a mutation · the six
stale team records of section E.

## I. Evidence + baseline rules (repo gates)

- Gates: `bun test packages`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test:qa`, `node scripts/verify-vendor.mjs`, and a
  `dsh --profile headless --dump-config` boot in an isolated `DSH_HOME`.
- Every lifecycle exercise runs with `HOME=<sandbox>` (the workmate library lives under HOME) and the sandbox path
  is asserted in the evidence. The real `~/.dsh` and the real HOME are never touched.
- Evidence on disk: `evidence/<domain>/<slug>/<timestamp>/{result.json,output.log}`.
- **BASELINE:** the tree is dirty by design — HEAD `f697088` plus 33 uncommitted entries from a previous session's

- Docs are BILINGUAL: every human-facing doc needs both `*.md` and `*.zh-CN.md` updated in the same change, each
  with the language switch link under its title. `AGENTS.md` is English-only.
"}
